A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AdaTTT research work and complete, readable 17-page manuscripts, including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparison establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrospective ICU experiments on Sites A/B and MIMIC-IV, including AUC and Brier results in Tables 1–2 and ablation and sensitivity results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original ICU prediction experiments, numerical comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B.2 retain identical architecture, reconstruction and masked-feature objectives, dynamic masking, prototype learning, partial optimal transport, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: The evaluated cohorts and task coverage are unchanged: Sites A/B and MIMIC-IV for 24-hour IMV prediction. The conclusion's mention of AKI and mortality is already present in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain TEST, CoTTA, T3A, SAR, TENT, TTT, TTT++, ClusT3, NC-TTT, PriTTT, and DynTTT. Appendix comparisons and baseline adaptations are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain identical cohort sizes and periods, preprocessing, labeling, evaluation metrics, hyperparameter-search procedures, and five-step test-time adaptation with per-instance reset.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C retain the same iteration-count, sequential-update, prototype-size, prototype-learning, masking, SSL-objective, and hyperparameter analyses. Patient and feature-importance examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard error over 20 independent test-time training runs in Section 4.1. Uncertainty reporting throughout the results is identical.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted results match, including Appendix C. Table 1 retains AdaTTT AUCs of 85.02±0.05, 84.10±0.05, and 77.17±0.08 for Site A, Site B, and MIMIC-IV, respectively.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Lemma 1, Theorem 2, mathematical definitions, and binary and multiclass derivations in Section 3.2 and Appendix A are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about information-theoretic bounds, feature-aware self-supervision, prototype-guided adaptation, and predictive performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of baseline and ablation results, sequential-adaptation degradation, and limitations concerning extreme conditional shifts and computational overhead are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details in Section 4.1 and Appendix B, computational timings, and the promised future release of code and configurations are identical. No reproducibility information or resource access is added.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the manuscript, and the reference list are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to clinical prediction and test-time adaptation research.

P1.justification: Only the administrative first-page stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 7 December 2025 to v2 dated 27 January 2026. Manuscript wording, title, authors, headings, and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; rendered differences are confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A–C retain identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information. Updating only the administrative arXiv stamp produces no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
